rundown: Breakers beat Bullets 94-90 (OT). It was level at 40-40 at the half. The 2nd quarter decided it: Breakers won it 26-16.
Leading the way — Bullets: Tyrell Harrison 22 pts; Raul Neto 10 ast; Nate Hinton 14 reb. Breakers: Dejan Vasiljevic 36 pts; Carlin Davison 13 ast, 12 reb.
Where Breakers won it: they turned it over 10 times to 14.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 13, 1:29 AM ET. It had Bullets 30% and Breakers 70%, projecting Bullets 89 – Breakers 95.1 (184 total, Breakers by 6.1).

Final: Bullets 90 – Breakers 94. Right winner: it had Breakers at 70%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Bullets came in with a 3% below average attack and a 2% leakier than average defense (6-6, 94.9 scored and 99.3 allowed a game over 12 games), worth about 24 and 24 games of evidence. Projected to score 89, they scored 90 (+1 points, 1% over); projected to allow 95.1, they allowed 94 (−1.1 points, 1% under).

Breakers came in with a 4% below average attack and a 3% stingier than average defense (4-8, 89.4 scored and 89.9 allowed a game over 12 games), worth about 24 and 24 games of evidence. Projected to score 95.1, they scored 94 (−1.1 points, 1% under); projected to allow 89, they allowed 90 (+1 points, 1% over).

The bigger miss was Breakers' scoring (-1.1 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 184 against 184 projected (0), about the 50th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±16).

Margin: Breakers by 4 against Breakers by 6.1 projected, about the 43rd percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±12).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection landed within its normal range anyway, so the flags didn't cost it much this time.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.003 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -2.8 points. It counts toward Hoops+ scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 38 graded Hoops+ games the algo now scales scoring ×1.003 and gives home teams -0.7 points. Team corrections start after 3 graded games for a team.

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
